newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Orient-Avia stops scheduled flights.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Orient-Avia stops scheduled flights.

text.p: Private Russian airline AO Orient-Avia has cancelled all scheduled passenger flights since July 10, but is continuing to operate charter flights, a company spokeswoman said on Friday.
"We have cancelled all scheduled flights from Moscow to Vladivostok and Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky as well as booking and selling of tickets to these flights," she told Reuters.
She declined to say why the airline was in difficulties and other company officials could not be contacted.
But a Federal Aviation Service (FAS) senior official said the Orient-Avia crisis had begun on July 10 after one of its Ilyushin Il-62 jets developed serious engine problems.
"It was the beginning of a chain of troubles for the airline," Yevgeny Lobachev, FAS's head of certification department, said.
Lobachev said Moscow-based carrier Domodedovo Airlines was carrying some of Orient-Avia's stranded passengers between Moscow and Petropavlovsk and Vladivostok.
About 1,500 Orient-Avia tickets have been sold on flights booked between July 10 and August 31, another FAS official said. Lobachev said he hoped all these passengers would be carried by September 1.
He was unable to say how many passengers were currently stranded at Moscow's Sheremetyevo-1 airport, waiting for flights to the Far East.
Orient-Avia, set up in 1994, carried 161,000 passengers and 1,560 tonnes of cargo and mail in 1996, up from 95,800 passengers and 860 tonnes of cargo and mail in 1995.
Last month Orient-Avia and East Line Air announced they had merged to create a new airline, East Line Aviation. Officials from East Line Air and the new merged airline were not available for comment.
